nodes.title: the Bramorn signature
nodes.statement: The Bramorn system concerns objects called zelbras. There are exactly 4 of them: tarnnyr, cloxil, isktez, iskmi. Two operations are written * and -. One relation is written <~, read as "shadows".

nodes.title: the Bramorn combination tables
nodes.statement: The value of x * y for every pair of zelbras is fixed by the table of the first operation, and likewise for -. The pairs standing in the <~ relation are listed in full.

nodes.title: closure under the first operation
nodes.statement: For all zelbras x and y, x * y is again a zelbra.

nodes.title: closure under the second operation
nodes.statement: For all zelbras x and y, x - y is again a zelbra.

nodes.title: association of the second operation
nodes.statement: For all zelbras x, y, z: (x - y) - z = x - (y - z).

nodes.title: commutation of the second operation
nodes.statement: For all zelbras x and y: x - y = y - x.

nodes.title: a neutral object for the second operation
nodes.statement: There is a zelbra tarnnyr with tarnnyr - x = x for every x.

nodes.title: self combination under the second operation
nodes.statement: For every zelbra x: x - x = x.

nodes.title: reflexivity of the relation
nodes.statement: For every zelbra x: x <~ x.

nodes.title: antisymmetry of the relation
nodes.statement: For all zelbras x and y: if x <~ y and y <~ x then x = y.

nodes.title: transitivity of the relation
nodes.statement: For all zelbras x, y, z: if x <~ y and y <~ z then x <~ z.

nodes.title: comparability of every pair
nodes.statement: For all zelbras x and y, at least one of x <~ y and y <~ x holds.

nodes.title: agreement of the relation with the second operation
nodes.statement: For all zelbras x, y, z: if x <~ y then (z - x) <~ (z - y) and (x - z) <~ (y - z).

nodes.title: the system does not have association of the first operation
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For all zelbras x, y, z: (x * y) * z = x * (y * z).

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = cloxil, y = tarnnyr, z = cloxil, left = tarnnyr, right = cloxil, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: pyrtez zelbras
nodes.statement: A zelbra x is called pyrtez when x * x = x.

nodes.title: zelbras that vorazt
nodes.statement: Two zelbras x and y are said to vorazt when x * y = y * x.

nodes.title: naknak collections
nodes.statement: A collection S of zelbras is naknak when x * y belongs to S for every pair x, y drawn from S.

nodes.title: the opalpyr of a zelbra
nodes.statement: The opalpyr of a zelbra x is the collection of zelbras y for which x <~ y holds.

nodes.title: the zelquil
nodes.statement: The zelquil of the system is the collection of zelbras that vorazt with every zelbra.

nodes.title: the rastmorn
nodes.statement: The rastmorn is the collection of all pyrtez zelbras.

nodes.title: the vintka of a zelbra
nodes.statement: The vintka of a zelbra x, written [x], is the smallest naknak collection that contains x.

nodes.title: a nakpyr
nodes.statement: A zelbra f is a nakpyr when f <~ y holds for every zelbra y, that is, when the opalpyr of f is the whole system.

nodes.title: the jenfal of a zelbra
nodes.statement: The jenfal of a zelbra x is the number of zelbras in its vintka [x].

nodes.title: the cloopal
nodes.statement: The cloopal of the system is the collection of zelbras whose jenfal is largest.

nodes.title: mishen pairs
nodes.statement: Two distinct zelbras x and y form a mishen pair when x <~ y and y <~ x both hold, that is, when each lies in the opalpyr of the other.

nodes.title: the vintka of a zelbra is naknak
nodes.statement: For every zelbra x, the collection [x] is naknak.

verification.domain: every object, then every pair inside its span
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: [x] is built by taking x and closing under *.
Closing under an operation is exactly the sealing condition.
The carrier is finite, so the closure stops after finitely many rounds.

nodes.title: the vintka is contained in every naknak collection
nodes.statement: If S is naknak and contains x, then S contains all of [x].

verification.domain: every sealed collection against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Every member of [x] is reached from x by finitely many applications of the operation.
A sealed S containing x is closed under each of those applications.
So each member of [x] is in S, by induction on the number of applications.

nodes.title: a zelbra is pyrtez exactly when its jenfal is one
nodes.statement: x * x = x holds if and only if [x] contains x alone.

verification.domain: every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: If x * x = x then {x} is already closed under *.
So [x] = {x} and the jenfal is one.
Conversely a span of one object must contain x * x, which is then x.

nodes.title: the jenfal divides the number of zelbras
nodes.statement: For every zelbra x, the jenfal of x divides 4.

verification.domain: every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: [x] is a naknak collection.
Its size is the jenfal of x.
The claim is that this size always divides 4.

nodes.title: the rastmorn is naknak
nodes.statement: If x and y are both pyrtez then so is x * y.

verification.domain: every ordered pair drawn from the ridge
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let x and y be pyrtez.
The claim asks whether (x * y) * (x * y) returns x * y.
Whether it does is settled by running the operation table on every such pair.

nodes.title: opalpyrs are nested along the relation
nodes.statement: If y lies in the opalpyr of x, then the opalpyr of y is contained in the opalpyr of x.

verification.domain: every ordered triple
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let y satisfy x <~ y and let z satisfy y <~ z.
Transitivity gives x <~ z.
So every member of the opalpyr of y is a member of that of x.

nodes.title: there is at most one nakpyr
nodes.statement: No two distinct zelbras can both be nakpyrs.

verification.domain: every candidate against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let f and h both be floors.
Then f <~ h, since h is any object, and h <~ f likewise.
Antisymmetry forces f = h.

nodes.title: the system has a nakpyr
nodes.statement: Some zelbra nakpyrs the whole system.

verification.domain: every candidate against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Every pair is comparable, so the relation orders the objects into a line.
The claim is that the line has a bottom.
The carrier is finite, so the search over candidates terminates.

nodes.title: no mishen pairs exist
nodes.statement: No two distinct zelbras lie in each other's opalpyr.

verification.domain: every ordered pair
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Suppose x and y form a tight pair.
Antisymmetry then identifies x with y.
So a tight pair of distinct objects cannot arise.
